calls.reason: The GPT-3 paper confirms coherence loss over long passages, and the planning studies (TattleTale, Re3) improve story coherence. None of them isolates the three proposed causes or tests grounding in the real world.

Li, Nye and Andreas (2021) use dynamic semantics to probe what language models represent, which counts against 'ignores all'. But it is one analysis paper, not the model-building approach, so the call depends on interpretation.

TruthfulQA shows models often give false answers, and GopherCite shows that citing sources did not make answers more truthful. Neither study tests whether neglecting reference, cognitive models or compositionality is the cause.

EntNet and Dreamer do keep and use internal state, but only in simplified stories and control tasks. 'Don't really… any of that' is loose rhetoric that also covers literary understanding, so the counterexamples don't clearly settle it.
A BERT probe separated literal from idiomatic uses with high accuracy, while GPT-3 interpreted metaphors unevenly. Neither directly tests context-driven switching against a human baseline.
LaMDA's retrieval tools produced source-attributed responses, which shows an external connection at the system level. That doesn't settle the claim about situated reference in standalone models.
